item.title: Business: As Relations With France Strain, Algeria Broadens Its Grain Suppliers
item.description: Algeria’s expanding wheat supplier list, including increased engagement with Canada, reflects a broader effort to reduce long-standing dependence on France as bilateral relations remain strained, turning food procurement into a quiet tool of economic recalibration.

item.title: Egypt Bets on Upstream Investment to Reverse Gas Production Decline
item.description: Egypt plans a major expansion of oil and gas exploration over the next five years as it seeks to stabilize natural gas output, restore export capacity, and integrate hydrocarbons into a broader energy transition strategy.

item.title: الجزائر: من داخل مشروع قانون سحب الجنسية الجزائر: من داخل مشروع قانون سحب الجنسية
item.description: يناقش البرلمان الجزائري مشروع قانون يتيح سحب الجنسية في حالات تُعدّ خطيرة على أمن الدولة أو وحدتها، بما يشمل أفعالًا تُرتكب داخل البلاد أو خارجها، مع تركيز خاص على المقيمين في الخارج والتعاون مع جهات أجنبية معادية.

item.title: الجزائر تعتزم إطلاق تجديد جواز السفر الرقمي للمواطنين المقيمين في الخارج
item.description: تستعد الجزائر لإطلاق نظام رقمي لتجديد جوازات السفر للمواطنين المقيمين في الخارج قبل نهاية عام 2025، بما يتيح تجديد الجوازات المنتهية الصلاحية عن بُعد اعتمادًا على البيانات البيومترية المتوفرة لدى القنصليات. ويُتوقع أن يخفف هذا الإجراء الضغط على القنصليات ويحسن وصول الجالية إلى الخدمات الإدارية.

item.title: Trump’s Expanded Travel Ban Targets Several African States
item.description: The Trump administration has quietly widened its travel‑ban system, adding partial restrictions on nationals from Mauritania, Nigeria, Senegal, Côte d’Ivoire, and several other African states.

item.title: Africa’s Exposure to the Russia–Ukraine Conflict Through Irregular Recruitment
item.description: A growing pattern of foreign recruitment into the Russia–Ukraine war is drawing increased scrutiny across Africa. Multiple cases indicate that African nationals, including Kenyans and South Africans, have been recruited under false pretenses, promised civilian or technical work in Russia and later diverted into military roles.

item.title: Algeria: Rail, Water, and Transport Drive 2026 Infrastructure Spending
item.description: Algeria’s 2026 finance law points to a renewed infrastructure investment cycle centered on rail transport, water systems, and national connectivity. item.title: Air Algérie Expands Long-Haul Capacity With Second A330-900neo
item.description: Air Algérie has added a second Airbus A330-900neo to its fleet as part of a gradual long-haul renewal program. The aircraft has been assigned to routes linking Algiers with Dubai, Beijing, and Guangzhou, reflecting a focus on maintaining capacity on established intercontinental markets rather than rapid network expansion.

item.title: Podcast: Development Without Aid: Power, Politics, and Local Resilience in the Global South
item.description: A conversation with Dr. Kate Schecter, President and CEO of World Neighbors, on how community-led development works in practice across the Global South.
